newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Repair kit ready for Mir, mission control says.
newsitem.headline: Repair kit ready for Mir, mission control says.

text.p: Russian experts have prepared all the equipment needed to repair the damaged Mir space station and will ship it to the Baikonur launchpad later on Monday, a senior space official said.

The deputy head of the mission, Vladimir Solovyov, told reporters the Progress cargo craft was due to be launched from there on July 5. The Russian-American crew are to repair the power supply. He said they would leave the job of sealing a hole in the Spektr science module to a fresh team.

Solovyov said 20 electric cables, hermetic electric connections and a specially-devised "hermoplate" needed for station power supply repairs would be sent by plane to Baikonur in the steppes of Kazakhstan at 2.00 p.m. (1000 GMT).
He confirmed the launch of cargo ship Progress M-35 with the equipment had now been set for July 5. It is due to dock with Mir on July 7.

But Solovyov said the present crew would only inspect the holed module from the inside, while the hole in Spektr would be patched by the next crew. Another cargo craft holed Spektr in a docking accident last Wednesday.
"This crew has not been trained to do this kind of repairs (sealing). The work is really difficult," Solovyov said. "Hermetic sealing will be done by a new crew, due to replace this one in August."
